name: Rhode Island
dueDateNotes: Rhode Island follows the federal schedule: April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15. If a due date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day.
selfEmploymentNotes: Rhode Island applies graduated rates (3.75%, 4.75%, 5.99%) to your federal AGI after a combined standard deduction and personal exemption ($10,900 + $5,100 = $16,000 for a single filer; $21,800 + two $5,100 exemptions = $32,000 for a married couple). Single and married filers use the same brackets. Note: at high incomes (roughly $246,000-$275,000 of AGI, 2024 figures) the standard deduction and exemptions phase out to zero; this calculator does not model that phase-out, so it can understate tax for very high earners.
uniqueFacts: Rhode Island uses the same tax brackets for single and married-filing-jointly filers, which creates a marriage penalty for two-earner couples.
Rhode Island is one of the few states that can tax Social Security benefits, following the federal taxable amount, though lower-income retirees qualify for a full exemption.
Rhode Island phases out its standard deduction and personal exemptions entirely for high earners, so the effective tax rate climbs faster than the posted 5.99% top rate suggests.
